claims.text: Localized nanoindentation testing on FeNiCrMn HEAs will reveal mechanical responses distinct from those of conventional steels.
The distinct mechanical responses of FeNiCrMn HEAs are attributable to their compositional and microstructural features.
The FeNiCrMn samples should be homogenized or as-cast and polished to a mirror finish.
Instrumented nanoindentation should be performed at multiple sample-surface sites using controlled load and loading rate.
Testing should use a standard Berkovich indenter under quasi-static, room-temperature ambient conditions.
Local lattice distortion affects dislocation motion and nanoscale mechanical response in FeNiCrMn HEAs.
The local distribution of stacking-fault energy affects dislocation motion and nanoscale mechanical response in FeNiCrMn HEAs.
Nanoindentation measures localized hardness and indentation elastic modulus.
Localized nanoindentation isolates the effect of high configurational entropy on the mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn HEAs.
FeNiCrMn HEAs will exhibit local hardness that is higher than or equivalent to that of conventional steels under identical nanoindentation parameters.
FeNiCrMn HEAs will exhibit deformation behavior distinct from conventional steels under identical nanoindentation parameters.
The expected nanoindentation response reflects enhanced or spatially heterogeneous strength in FeNiCrMn HEAs.
The measured differences may depend on the exact FeNiCrMn composition and microstructural state.
Nanoindentation results from one processing state cannot be extrapolated to all FeNiCrMn processing routes without validation.
Local hardness variations cannot yet be assumed to represent bulk-scale properties across diverse processing states and temperatures.
A 316L stainless-steel reference tested under identical preparation and nanoindentation conditions can serve as the control.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits hardness equivalent to conventional steel, whereas the falsification rule treats the absence of a statistically significant hardness increase or distinct hardness distribution as falsifying. Thus, an equivalent-hardness result can be both predicted and falsifying.
